Exact point-in-polygon indicators per place

Source: R/place_exact.R
obis_place_indicators_exact.Rd

Computes the biodiversity indicators of each place of a polygon collection (EEZs, offshore regions, sanctuaries, ...) from the OBIS occurrences that fall inside the polygon, tested point by point with DuckDB's spatial extension, with no H3 approximation. This complements obis_place_indicators(), which pools area-weighted H3 cells.

Usage

obis_place_indicators_exact(
  occ,
  places,
  eov = NULL,
  decades = TRUE,
  years = TRUE,
  esn = 50L,
  max_vertices = 256L,
  con = NULL,
  memory_limit = NULL,
  threads = NULL,
  temp_dir = NULL,
  max_temp_dir_size = NULL,
  s3_region = "us-east-1",
  s3_anonymous = TRUE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  grid_deg = NULL
)

Arguments

occ

the occurrences: a data.frame with decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude, species and optionally date_year, records and aphiaid (needed for eov), or parquet path(s)/glob(s) of OBIS open data (s3:// URLs too), either the nested layout (DwC fields in an interpreted struct) or flat. The schema is probed from one file.

places

the places: an sf object, or the path(s) of GeoParquet file(s), with a place_id column and polygon geometry (WKB geometry), e.g. a gazetteer places.parquet. An optional area_km2 column is used for density; without it the geodesic area is computed from the geometry (ST_Area_Spheroid). place_id must be unique.

eov

EOV membership for the eov rows: NULL (none), a data frame with columns eov and taxonID (matched to aphiaid), or a DBI connection to a store with an eov table (see obis_eov_bake()).

decades

decades (first year) to compute besides all years: TRUE (default) for 1960-2020 as in the export, FALSE or NULL for none, or an integer vector.

years

per-year rows: TRUE (default) every year with records, FALSE or NULL none, or an integer vector of years.

esn

expected sample size for ES(n); default 50.

max_vertices

the most vertices a polygon piece may have before it is cut into quadrants (default 256, at least 8). It only affects speed and memory, not results.

con

optional DuckDB connection to use (the spatial extension is loaded into it); default a private in-memory one. Temporary tables are dropped on exit.

memory_limit, threads, temp_dir, max_temp_dir_size

DuckDB resource guards, as in build_obis_h3_duckdb(). Pass them for a global parquet scan, which otherwise can exhaust RAM.

s3_region, s3_anonymous

for s3:// sources, as in build_obis_h3_duckdb().

verbose

message progress.

grid_deg

deprecated and ignored (the polygons used to be clipped to a grid); a message is shown when it is given.

Value

a list with

  • indicators: one row per place x eov ("all" or the EOV) x decade (NA = all years) with records: place_id, eov, decade, n (records), sp (species), shannon, simpson (sum of p^2), es (ES(esn), NA where n < esn), hill_1 (exp(shannon)), hill_2 (1 / simpson), bp (Berger-Parker, max(ni) / n, the maxp of calc_indicators()) and density (n / area_km2, records per km2).

  • years: the same per place x eov x year.

  • diagnostics: records_in (records summed over the places, all taxa and years), records_out (filtered records outside every place), records_total (filtered records), records_in_unique (records_total - records_out, records_in without double counting overlaps), overlaps (a list: n locations that match more than one place, their place_ids and records), n_places, n_places_with_records, n_locations (distinct locations), n_pieces, max_vertices, max_piece_vertices (the largest piece) and subdivision_rounds.

Without overlapping places, records_in + records_out == records_total.

Details

The method:

  1. Occurrence filters as build_obis_h3_duckdb(): species, decimalLatitude and decimalLongitude not null; dropped and absence not true. Records are grouped by (longitude, latitude, aphiaid, species, year), records being the row count (or the sum of a records column when the source has one).

  2. Place pieces: each polygon is dumped into its parts (so a place split at +/-180 becomes local parts with local bounding boxes), and every part with more than max_vertices vertices is cut into the four quadrants of its own bounding box (ST_Intersection, empties dropped, parts dumped again), round after round until every piece is small. The spatial join then tests points against small pieces instead of rings with hundreds of thousands of vertices. Each round is a table (so DuckDB can spill) and copies a geometry at most four times; at most 24 rounds, else an error.

  3. Join: each distinct location is matched to the pieces with ST_Intersects (DuckDB's R-tree spatial join) and then to its place_id. A location on the shared boundary of two places matches both; these are counted in diagnostics$overlaps and warned about.

  4. Indicators per place, by EOV ("all" plus each EOV in eov) and by decade (all years, then each of decades) or by year, with the shared indicator SQL (the ES(esn) term of the parity contract is untouched).

Polygons must be valid (no self-intersections); a point exactly on a polygon edge counts as inside.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- obis_place_indicators_exact(
  "/data/obis/occurrence/*.parquet", "~/data/places/mr_eez/places.parquet",
  eov = obis_store_connect("~/data/obis/obis_h3.duckdb"),
  memory_limit = "16GB", threads = 6, temp_dir = "/data/tmp")
obis_place_exact_write(res, "~/data/obis-h3/v20261020", "mr_eez")
} # }
